source.title: GCSE subject content and national curriculum mathematics programmes of study

units.title: Number: integers, fractions and standard form
units.description: Use integers, fractions, recurring decimals, powers, roots and standard form accurately in GCSE-style problems.
units.generationNotes: Use exact calculations where possible and state calculator assumptions. Cover fractions, indices, roots, standard form and bounds without relying on unseen diagrams.

objectives.text: Apply numerical methods with integers, fractions, powers, roots and standard form.

units.title: Algebra: expressions, equations and sequences
units.description: Manipulate expressions, solve equations and inequalities, and recognise sequences using clear algebraic reasoning.
units.generationNotes: Show every algebraic transformation. Include expanding, factorising, linear and quadratic equations, inequalities and sequences at an appropriate GCSE level.

objectives.text: Use algebraic notation to manipulate expressions, solve equations and inequalities, and describe sequences.

units.title: Ratio, proportion and rates of change
units.description: Solve direct and inverse proportion, scale, percentage change and rate problems in mathematical and realistic contexts.
units.generationNotes: Use exact, fully stated contexts. Distinguish direct from inverse proportion and show units for rates. Avoid financial advice; money examples are fictional calculations only.

objectives.text: Solve problems involving ratio, proportion, scale, percentage change and rates of change.

units.title: Geometry: properties, congruence and similarity
units.description: Use angle facts, shape properties, congruence, similarity and circle theorems to justify geometric conclusions.
units.generationNotes: Describe every diagram in words or provide all dimensions. Require reasons for angle and similarity results; do not ask learners to infer an unseen image.

objectives.text: Use geometric properties, angle relationships, congruence, similarity and circle theorems to solve problems.

units.title: Geometry: measures, area, volume and trigonometry
units.description: Calculate perimeter, area, surface area and volume, and apply Pythagoras and trigonometry to fully specified shapes.
units.generationNotes: State dimensions and units explicitly. Show square and cubic units, calculator mode where relevant, and identify the chosen trigonometric ratio.

objectives.text: Calculate measures of shapes and use Pythagoras and trigonometry in right-angled and non-right-angled contexts.

units.title: Probability: combined events and representations
units.description: Calculate and interpret probabilities for single and combined events using sample spaces, tree diagrams and Venn diagrams.
units.generationNotes: State independence or conditional information explicitly. Give all branches or sets in text if no diagram is rendered, and distinguish mutually exclusive from overlapping events.

objectives.text: Represent and calculate probabilities for single and combined events, including conditional situations.

units.title: Statistics: sampling, averages and data
units.description: Interpret tables and charts, compare distributions and use averages, spread and sampling ideas to draw cautious conclusions.
units.generationNotes: Use compact fictional data supplied in the prompt. Explain misleading samples, correlation versus causation, averages and spread without claiming certainty from limited data.

objectives.text: Interpret and analyse data using statistical measures, representations, sampling and reasoned conclusions.

units.title: Graphs and functions: linear, quadratic and real-life models
units.description: Plot, interpret and transform graphs, including linear and quadratic relationships and graphs describing real-life change.
units.generationNotes: Provide equations, coordinates or a verbal description rather than relying on an unseen graph. Include gradient, intercept, roots, transformations or rates of change with clear working.

objectives.text: Use graphs and functions to represent, interpret and solve mathematical and real-life problems.
